name: ARIMA / SARIMA
summary: Models a single time series from its own past values and past forecast errors, with optional seasonal terms.
inputs: One regularly spaced univariate series; optional exogenous regressors (SARIMAX).
outputs: Point forecasts with prediction intervals; fitted parameters and residual diagnostics.

data_requirements.min_observations: About 50+ points; several seasonal cycles for SARIMA
data_requirements.missing_values: Handled by the state-space likelihood in statsmodels

assumptions: Series is stationary after differencing (d, D)
Linear dependence on past values and past errors
Constant error variance (otherwise pair with GARCH)
math_summary: phi(B)Phi(B^s)(1-B)^d(1-B^s)^D y_t = theta(B)Theta(B^s) e_t: autoregressive and moving-average polynomials in the backshift operator B, with optional seasonal terms of period s.
when_to_use: Single series with clear autocorrelation and seasonality
Short to medium histories where deep models overfit
when_not_to_use: Many related series that benefit from shared learning
Multiple seasonalities (e.g. hourly electricity) without extra structure
pitfalls: Choosing orders by in-sample fit only; compare with out-of-sample errors

compute.complexity: Fitting via Kalman-filter likelihood, roughly O(n * state_dim^2) per iteration.
compute.hardware: CPU, milliseconds to seconds per series.

applicability.use_case: Forecasting monthly federal receipts or outlays
Seasonal forecasting of monthly employment or price indices
